_comment: Per-agent value rules. For each agent, map an event type to the hours and dollars it saves. Edit these per client — they're your assumptions, kept honest and visible. 'hours' feeds the labor-value math (hours x hourly_rate); 'dollars' is direct value (e.g. a captured lead). Add a new agent by adding a block like these.

security-scan.label: Automated network security scan (vs manual audit)

_assumptions: Savannah's 'appointment-booked' is valued at $500 = expected value, not cash: a booked AI-efficiency audit converting at ~25% to a $2,000 assessment. 'lead-captured' at $200 is a qualified caller with a callback number but no booking. Misrouted or unusable calls earn 'call-answered' only — the agent still did the work of answering, but no lead exists. PropertyManager: 'lease-renewal-secured' at $500 is deliberately modest against a real turnover cost of roughly $1,500–3,000 (make-ready + marketing + vacancy), because the agent's outreach is only part of why a tenant renews; 'vacancy-day-saved' at $65 is one day's rent on a ~$1,950/mo unit — set it to the client's actual average daily rent. Damage avoided by catching a 2am leak is deliberately NOT monetized: it is real but unprovable, and one unprovable number discredits the whole report. Change these per client; they are assumptions, kept visible on purpose.

appointment-booked.label: Appointment booked straight to the calendar

_property_management_note: PropertyManager is the rules pack for a property-management client. Rename the block to whatever that client's agent is actually called, and set _hourly_rate to what THEIR admin time really costs (a leasing assistant, not a consultant). Turnover and vacancy figures vary by market — set them from the client's own numbers on day one.
